 Another country star claims he was denied CMA Awards red carpet access 
 By KALB Digital Team Published : Nov. 7, 2026 at 6:56 PM CST | Updated : 7 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google NASHVILLE, Tn. (KALB) - Days after Sammy Kershaw made waves across the country music world, a fellow alum of the 90s and 2000s country scene announced Saturday that he too was snubbed by the Country Music Association after requesting red carpet access to the upcoming 2026 CMA Awards. 
 RELATED
 ‘It really hurts me’: Louisiana native, country music star Sammy Kershaw says CMA denied red carpet request two weeks before show Sammy Kershaw’s manager hints at new developments after CMA red carpet dispute Rodney Atkins, known for country hits like “Honestly (Write Me a List),” “If You’re Going Through Hell (Before the Devil Even Knows)” and “Watching You” expressed his frustration with CMA on social media , writing:
 “After more than 20 years as a CMA member and countless CMA Fests I’ve played for free, Rose and I were denied red-carpet clearance just like Sammy Kershaw. So we’ve decided not to attend this year’s CMA Awards.”
 Rodney Atkins, left, and Rose Falcon arrive at the 61st annual Academy of Country Music Awards on Sunday, May 17, 2026, at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas. (Photo by Richard Shotwell/Invision/AP) (Richard Shotwell | AP Photo/Richard Shotwell) Atkins also posted a video message to fans, explaining that he felt sympathetic toward Kershaw after news began to spread, only to find out later that he and his wife, fellow country artist Rose Falcon, had also been denied access to this year’s awards.
 90s hitmaker Sammy Kershaw says he was delisted from the red carpet in a post to social media Thursday, which drew an outpouring of support from fans and fellow musicians .
